doc.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014

title: Awards late in life and making a living playing what he loved
summary: Heath feels fortunate to have lived off music he loved, admitting some compromise while at Columbia Records.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah. You know since the 80s and so forth you have garnered some wonderful awards, some commissions, honorary degrees. Do you sometimes think I could have used some of that in the 1960s?

Well you know as far as — I feel very fortunate to have made a living off of playing what I like. Not a lot of people can say that. You have to compromise, and I have at one point when we were with Columbia Records we compromised and added some things to sell more product. But basically I would say I’ve been very fortunate to play the music I loved all my life and made a good living.
And written some lasting compositions too.
I think so. I hope so.
